recent_lessons.lesson: Thu Sep 10 pre-open — PPI day into a 3-day sell streak. S&P 7,636.36 (-0.48%), Nasdaq 26,253.34 (-0.64%), Dow 52,380.66 (-0.77%) — third consecutive decline across benchmarks. PPI printed 5.3% (vs 4.7% prior, +0.6pp acceleration), confirming inflation is re-accelerating into the supply shock. 10Y 4.845% (+4bp, highest since Nov 2023), 30Y 5.295%, 2Y 4.436%, VIX 16.46 (+4.71%). Brent crude reclaimed $101.21 (+3.36%) as IRGC announced a new maritime sanction zone and US struck Iranian oil tankers — the Hormuz blockade regime is hardening, not easing. Treasury buyback of $6B in 10-20Y bonds fell below $7-8B expectations, compounding yield pressure. ACN $178.03 (+1.27% from $175.80 close) — recovering from yesterday's GPT-6 Astra software-disruption selloff but still below the $178-188 range of prior weeks. Fed hike odds ~70%. CPI tomorrow (Sep 11), FOMC Sep 15-16. The tightening-into-supply-shock regime is now in its 10th day — PPI acceleration + oil above $100 + yields at 3-year highs = the ratchet keeps tightening, no release valve visible before CPI/FOMC. ACN BULLISH thesis holding at 2.3% unrealized gain vs $174.00 entry; the thesis is being tested by macro forces (oil/rates) that are independent of ACN's fundamentals.

Sep 8 close — Houthis struck Saudi Aramco (73 wounded, temporary shutdowns), Brent hit six-week high $98.63 intraday / $97.31 settle, WTI $94.15. Dow -628pts (-1.18%), S&P -0.58%, Nasdaq -0.32%. ACN -4.12% to ~$178.24 (GPT-6 Astra software-disruption fears + oil/rates headwinds; YTD -31.4%). 10Y 4.764%, 2Y 4.362%, VIX 15.72. Gold $4,400 (-1.71%, rate-hike hedging). Fed Sep hike odds 57-60%. PPI Wed, CPI Thu, FOMC Sep 15-16. The tightening-into-supply-shock regime is active; ACN BULLISH thesis under real-world test at $178 vs $174 entry.

Global AI/chip washout hit FOMC-eve: KOSPI −10.84%, SK Hynix ~−15%, Nikkei −3.95%, Taiwan −4.65%, dragging Micron/Nvidia and pinning Nasdaq futures red (oil $80.6 −2.4%, 10Y 4.618%, VIX 18.9). Lesson: the AI-infra complex is one correlated trade — Nvidia-as-backstop 'circular financing' means chip-complex drawdowns cascade across the whole build-out. Size DOWN correlated AI-infra/semi exposure into tomorrow's FOMC decision (Wed Jul 29, 2pm ET) + megacap earnings week; value accrues to disciplined deployers who own demand + proprietary data, not leverage.

T-1 on the MCP stateless rewrite (ratifies Jul-28). Tomorrow the session handshake/init step is removed spec-wide — every write-capable connector The Construct runs is touched. Load-bearing move today: finish the migration + least-authority hardening inventory before the spec lands, not chase model news. Trade/venture read-through: keep the Jul-28 event hedge on agent-infra exposure and continue to favor approval-gated workflow vendors over full-autonomy plays through the transition.

MCP's Jul-28 stateless rewrite is now 2 days out — a breaking change touching every write-capable connector we run. The load-bearing move is the migration + least-authority hardening inventory before Tuesday, not chasing model news (quiet Sunday, no new Anthropic drop since Friday's Agentic AI Foundation donation). Trade read-through: keep the Jul-28 event hedge on agent-infra exposure; the structural de-risking (LF stewardship) is real but the execution event is near-term. Favor approval-gated workflow vendors over full-autonomy plays.

MCP moved to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation (co-founded w/ Block + OpenAI) the same week its Jul-28 stateless rewrite ratifies — the agent-infra standard just de-risked structurally, but the breaking change is a near-term execution event. Cut the platform-lock-in discount on agent-infra exposure; keep an event hedge into Jul-28. Corroborating tape: 'AI drafts, human approves' is now the validated SMB default (OpenAI Presence + market roundups) — favor approval-gated workflow vendors over full-autonomy plays.
HBR/HBS: value accrues to AI deployers not builders (1.8M-patent study, Srinivasan) — as the capex selloff broadens (Nasdaq -2.15%, TSLA -14.5%), price AI on demonstrated returns.

Lens tape: AI-capex 'spending shock' repriced the trade — GOOGL sank on a $205B 2026 capex guide despite a Q2 beat; CNBC read it 'spending shock disappoints Wall Street.' Signal: markets now price AI on demonstrated ROI, not optionality. WOLF bias — fade high-capex/low-return-visibility AI names into guidance, favor deployers capturing value.

Lens tape (CNBC): AI-trade capital rotated down-stack from compute to memory/storage/test — Sandisk +14.3%, WDC +12.5%, Micron +12.2%, Teradyne +12.1%, Coherent +11.1% led a broad risk-on session (S&P +0.89%, Nasdaq +1.29%). WOLF read: when GPU names cool, the marginal AI bid migrates to the physical substrate of inference (memory/storage/test) — watch that sub-sector for momentum continuation before assuming the AI trade is fading.

HBS WK (Kang): banks turn marketing-grade customer telemetry into a regional macro-forecasting signal — validates alt-data-as-signal; operationalize proprietary customer exhaust as a WOLF/Prism edge. Market read Jul 21: chip rebound failed in US cash (S&P 7,443 -0.19%) while Asia ripped overnight (KOSPI +3.56%, Taiwan +4.2%) — opposite signs across sessions is a timezone/liquidity artifact, not conviction; don't initiate on the overnight gap. Defensive bid corroborated (Dimon won't buy stocks or Treasurys; 10Y 4.60%; gold +1.29% $4,068, silver +4.17%). Keep AI-hardware longs short-leashed into Alphabet + Tesla prints.

Mon Jul 20 — tape is trading headlines, not a regime. The war-risk premium whipsawed fully out inside 48h (Iran halts strikes, WTI eases to $81.9 off the $82.47 spike; CNBC flips 'surge' → 'panic to pricing in'). Lesson for WOLF: fade single-headline geopolitical spikes that lack a durable supply/demand mechanism — size down, don't chase. Standing structural read into a heavy earnings week (Alphabet + Tesla): the silicon→systems AI rotation still owns the tape; chip names (Synopsys/Cadence/Intuitive) sit at the bottom of the movers board. Treat this week's mega-cap prints as the live test of whether that repricing is rotation or top; keep AI-hardware longs on a short leash until the prints confirm.

HBR/Markets: AI rotation (silicon->systems) owns the tape into Alphabet/Tesla earnings week — rotation vs top is the live test. Geopolitics whipsaws back to 'priced-in' inside 48h: Iran stops strikes on Israel, oil eases 82.47->81.9. War premium is headline-driven, not regime.

Sun Jul 19 (mkts closed) — the moat keeps migrating off the model and onto the harness + org structure. Today's convergent read: HBR names "brand debt" (AI touchpoints silently erode brand equity unless governed) while HBS AI Institute/Sana documents AI-companion exit-moment dark patterns carrying measurable churn + legal-liability cost — both say the durable asset is trust/governance, not raw capability. Industry Pulse echoes it: Claude Code hardens the harness (EndConversation, /verify + /code-review invoke-only, tighter permission scoping) and agent-harness engineering firms into a named field. WOLF takeaway: as chip enthusiasm keeps converting to ROI scrutiny (last week's silicon selloff), keep positioning toward services/platforms/power and verification-loop quality — the residual claimant is structure and human judgment, not the picks-and-shovels layer.

HBR: 'brand debt' — as AI mediates more customer touchpoints, un-governed AI accumulates a brand liability; lower-brand-debt firms win with AI. Macro: Mideast re-escalation (US deaths in Jordan, Iran calls off peace deal) re-hardens risk, oil +4.5%.

Sat Jul 18 (mkts closed) — the AI trade keeps repricing from silicon to systems: this week's chip selloff (Nikkei -4.03%, Shanghai -3.05%, HSI -1.78%, VIX +12.2% to 18.77, S&P -1.01%) is capex enthusiasm converting to ROI scrutiny across the stack. CNBC framing: own "services, platforms, power, not just picks and shovels." Convergent signal from HBR/Wharton/HBS/MIT — human judgment and org structure are the residual claimants as the model layer commoditizes (same shape as the cover-letter-decay lesson: vendor keeps the revenue, adopter loses the alpha). Macro risk is softening in parallel — Iran halted strikes on Israel, oil back below $100, 10Y yield falling. WOLF read: fade single-name silicon beta into the repricing, favor systems/power/platform exposure and durable-margin operators; treat any AI-derived edge as mean-reverting on adoption.
